mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows ApiCall atoms with no ac_caller (unauthenticated calls). The AuthRequiredEverywhere and FR_001_AuthRequired predicates both assert `all c: ApiCall | one c.ac_caller`, so Alloy will find a counterexample where an ApiCall atom has zero callers.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthenticatedCall { some c: ApiCall | no c.ac_caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the uniqueness constraint on td_task_ref across TaskDeletion atoms. The injection forces two distinct TaskDeletion entries with the same td_task_ref, which is exactly what AppendOnly, FR_012_PermanentDeletion, and FR_018_DeletionLogCorrectness assert cannot happen.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateDeletionEntry { some disj td1, td2: TaskDeletion | td1.td_task_ref = td2.td_task_ref }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that editing a Done task requires reopening it. The injection forces an EditRequest targeting a Done task without a reopening status, which is exactly the violation FR_011_ClosedTaskRule checks for.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskViolation { some er: EditRequest | er.er_target.t_status = Done and er.er_new_status = Done }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows the same task to appear in multiple TaskDeletion entries (or none). The injection forces exactly two deletion log entries for the same task, violating the lone-entry requirement that AuditCompleteness asserts.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateAuditEntry { some disj td1, td2: TaskDeletion | td1.td_task_ref = td2.td_task_ref }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows Task atoms with no creator. The injection forces a Task with no t_creator, violating OwnershipExclusivity's assertion that every task has exactly one creator.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OrphanTask { some t: Task | no t.t_creator }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows a Task to have an assignee that is not a Member. The injection forces a Task to have a non-null assignee field that does not resolve to any Member, which FR_008_AssigneeIsMember directly checks.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonMemberAssignee { some t: Task | some m: Member | t.t_assignee != m and some t.t_assignee }
